requirements.requirement: Add at least 512MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap on node1
requirements.summary: swapon --show and /proc/swaps confirm /dev/zram0 at 512M (536870912 bytes) with lz4 compression algorithm selected, and a memory-pressure test (cmd-118bd72f3ed04a35) confirmed the swap is actually usable, driving swap usage to 8.6M under ~900MB allocation on a 999MB-RAM node.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persists across reboot)
requirements.summary: zram-swap.service was enabled (symlinked into multi-user.target.wants and swap.target.wants) prior to reboot. A full reboot cycle was captured: pre-restart boot_id and healthy 512M zram swap (cmd-7a9fc9997d644a66), the shutdown command (cmd-9d60ea3c50ad4777), node unreachable twice (cmd-97ae5d9637354088, cmd-c97844af3ba24a8b), reconnection (cmd-380b13c66aff47ff), and post-restart confirmation of a new boot_id plus the service auto-started with 512M lz4 zram swap active at priority 100 (cmd-3332e99b8e1d495f). This matches the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot (75a9f473-7966-4168-a412-144ea086a8ad), corroborating an actual restart occurred.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: The zram device was configured with swap priority 100 (a high value ensuring precedence over typical default-priority disk swap), and /etc/fstab was confirmed to contain no swap entries, meaning no disk-backed swap exists to compete with it. Given the topology has no disk swap at all, the priority setting is sufficient to satisfy the 'preferred over any disk-backed swap' requirement as stated.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: a 512MB lz4-compressed zram swap device was created, verified functional under memory pressure, configured with priority 100 (with no competing disk-backed swap present), and confirmed to survive a full, directly-observed reboot cycle (pre-restart baseline, disconnection, reconnection, new boot_id, and recovered service/swap state). The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on the single managed node and aligns with the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified in the executor's command trace.
limitations: Preference over disk-backed swap could only be verified structurally (priority value, no fstab swap entries) since no disk-backed swap existed on this node to test against in a live competing scenario.
The zram-config Upstart package alternative was not used; the executor built a custom systemd unit, which is an equally valid implementation choice.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing all 20 chronological executor commands, every state-changing action has a clear purpose: apt-get update/install (cmd-269f2342673b4086, cmd-21efa610e7c041e3) was a necessary prerequisite to obtain the missing zram kernel module; modprobe zram (cmd-ccc575fc268441ae) and writing the systemd unit plus modules-load.d config (cmd-7f7b0cb9b7094169) directly implement the requirement; the swapoff/rmmod/daemon-reload/enable sequence (cmd-d74e5f77d8e7401b) is a bounded reset to ensure the manually-loaded module state didn't conflict with the new systemd-managed service before enabling it; starting the service (cmd-e632a2b1fb894720) and the reboot (cmd-9d60ea3c50ad4777) are required to configure and verify the outcome. The memory-pressure test (cmd-118bd72f3ed04a35) allocated transient memory that was freed when the Python process exited, leaving no residue. No unnecessary, abandoned, or destructive mutations were found; the after_executor snapshot shows no failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no package-health issues, consistent with clean execution. Temporary-file and package-health diffs between before_prepare and after_executor reflect only expected reboot-related systemd-private directories, not executor residue.
